title: Typed Response Contract Linting Pipeline for model/config rollouts
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: We currently lack an automated, low-latency check that ties model and config changes to field-level contract violations for typed/JSON responses during rollouts. Outages or subtle quality regressions have been caught manually or via coarse evals that do not map directly to rollout events or config diffs.

Goal: Build a pipeline (Typed Response Contract Linting Pipeline - TRCLP) that: 1) computes per-field schema/typing adherence and semantic sanity scores on a representative sample of production-like requests; 2) automatically compares new model/config rollout snapshots against the pinned baseline; and 3) emits a holistic pass/fail and per-field delta report that can gate canary rollouts and create Console alerts.

Scope: The initial MVP will focus on JSON object responses for API generation/chat endpoints with explicitly declared output contracts (OpenAPI-like schemas or JSON Schema). It will: - Run lightweight preflight evals on canary traffic plus synthetic prompts derived from customer prompt-sets; - Compute deterministic schema violations (missing fields, type mismatches, enum divergences) and soft quality deltas (e.g., field-level token entropy shifts, small-format regression heuristics); - Expose a scorecard and time-series for Console; - Integrate with rollout engine to allow automatic pause if weighted failure > threshold.

Non-goals: Full natural-language semantic correctness scoring (beyond basic heuristics) and long-tail log-based analysis (these belong to follow-ups).

Design notes: - Contract representation: use existing customer-declared JSON Schemas where available; otherwise synthesize a best-effort schema from sample responses and store as a pinned baseline per-route. - Differential engine: compute per-field metrics (violation_count, violation_rate, avg_token_entropy, avg_length, enum_changes). Combine into a weighted delta score with configurable weights per-route. - Sampling: mirror canary sampling + a small seeded synthetic corpus to surface edge cases. - Latency/Cost budget: preflight jobs must run under a 10s P90 per-request budget and limit token usage for synthetic prompts. - Outputs: a compact JSON delta report for programmatic gating and a human-readable table for Console.

Risk/trade-offs: - Conservative thresholds reduce false alarms but delay detection. We will provide a quick calibration UI to tune weights for critical routes. - Generating schemas automatically risks overfitting to a specific model's output; baseline pinning is critical.
acceptance_criteria: A stable TRCLP job can be triggered by the rollout controller for any model/config snapshot and produces a per-route JSON delta report within the rollout time window.
Per-field deterministic schema violations (missing field, wrong primitive type, enum mismatch) are detected and listed with examples in the report.
Delta scoring combines deterministic violations and soft heuristics into a single weighted score; default thresholds are documented and adjustable in Console.
Console shows the TRCLP scorecard for canaries and exposes a "pause rollout on failure" toggle that integrates with existing rollout policies.
A test harness with 200 synthetic examples and 1k mirrored canary requests reproduces at least two historical regressions used as benchmarks.
A minimal GitHub PR (link included in comments) implements the routing, job runner, and schema-diff module and passes unit/integration tests.
comments: 2025-02-18 - Aisha Patel: Created ticket after post-mortem showed two customer incidents where schema drift caused downstream deserialization failures. Referenced incident notes in Confluence: https://confluence.company/reports/schema-drift-postmortem

2025-02-21 - Marco Ruiz: Proposal for TRCLP data model uploaded to Drive: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/TRCLP-design. Decided to reuse route-level pinned schema concept from the Console team. Open question: how to represent optional vs absent fields in baseline.

2025-02-27 - Sophie Chen (review): Reviewed differential scoring approach. Suggested adding token-entropy and length-delta heuristics to catch truncation/regression. Also requested a privacy pass for synthetic prompt seeding.

2025-03-01 - Marco Ruiz: Implemented prototype schema linter and synthetic prompt generator. Early results: detected injected field rename in synthetic canary with a delta score of 0.83. Prototype PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/trclp/pull/12

2025-03-04 - Product (Liam O'Connor): Wants a default conservative threshold (failure if deterministic violation_rate > 0.5% OR combined delta_score > 0.6) and ability to override per-project. Added to acceptance criteria.
2025-03-05 - Marco Ruiz: Integration test run against canary pipeline OK (200 mirrored requests); next: wire Console toggle and rollout pause hook.
